patch_resolves_note: The staged `patch.diff` does not apply to the workspace checkout left by Stage 01, so Stage 04 used the authoritative `n132/arvo:16531-fix` image for fixed-side evidence. On that fixed image the original PoC runs clean and still reaches `second_decode_stop` genuinely with `size_mod_chr == 0` and `token_export.token_len == second_decode_stop.size_bytes == 10`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: First project statement that turns attacker-controlled input into the dispatch key for the vulnerable wide-decoder path.

The positive-length wide decode uses the raw byte count to form a `unsigned short *` stop pointer instead of validating and converting `size` into 2-byte element units; once `DocumentChecker` has already emitted a code-unit count as `tok.len`, an odd `size` makes the loop boundary unreachable.
ASan crash site in the second wide decode. Once the stop pointer from step 10 is unreachable, this dereference becomes the 2-byte read that crosses the end of the heap input buffer.

At the sink loop, `in` has advanced strictly past the caller-requested slice end `in0 + size`, so `out.append(*in)` dereferences beyond the requested span on the path that continues to the ASan heap overread.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable original trace records `second_decode_overread.read_addr > second_decode_overread.requested_end_addr` on every post-stop iteration, including the final dereference before ASan reports the heap-buffer-overflow.

nodes.description: Intermediate runtime event token_export materialized from verified transition assertion A-TOKEN-LEN-REACHES-SECOND-DECODE-SIZE.

edges.evidence: The frozen traces record `token_export.token_len == second_decode_stop.size_bytes` on both versions (5 on the vulnerable crash, 10 on the fixed original).
The vulnerable original trace records `second_decode_stop.stop_addr == second_decode_overread.stop_addr` across the first post-stop dereference.
